title: Preserve trim, codec delay and decoder preroll exactly once
finding: Current remux explicitly preserves Opus padding through WebM choice, records initial padding and retains bounded real seek preroll. R094 has scoped sample-boundary evidence, but there is no new proof here that all AAC/MP3/Opus mixed/chunked routes apply trim exactly once.
novelty: R094 is the exact trim/preroll owner; R060 captions was a provisional, unrelated link and is not adopted.
next_action: Use independently decoded impulse/channel-marked AAC, MP3 and Opus fixtures at head/tail and seek boundaries; declare each trim owner and sample units. Require exact counts/positions before admitting any new wrapper or split route.
reopen_condition: A wrapper must not silently discard side data it cannot represent. Preserve a working baseline or reject the new route when sample-accurate semantics are unavailable.

proposal_contract.Proposed mechanism: Keep audible sample bounds distinct from decoder input/recovery bounds. Use explicit rational/sample units and one responsible component for each trim or codec delay.
proposal_contract.Smallest useful experiment: Use impulses and channel labels around AAC/MP3/Opus head/tail boundaries; seek near the start and into a stream; compare one-shot decode with chunked/mixed-route output.
proposal_contract.Correctness gate: Reference sample count and impulse positions, no double trim or priming leakage, correct channel identities, and required recovery packets still supplied.
proposal_contract.Measure only after correctness: Audio correctness and additional component admission; CPU only after equivalent samples and policies match.

upstream_evidence: Imported 2026-09-21 source review, not fetched or revalidated in this run.
